column1: # Suite B (cli): the scenarios both launchers are run through, against a fake
# docker. Read by test/cli/run-cli.sh (./dev under sh, dash, busybox, Git Bash)
# and PowerShell 7, and ./dev under Git Bash with FakeDocker.exe). One table
# for every implementation is the point: dev and dev.ps1 are a pair, and this
# is what "the same behaviour" means, written down.
# TAB-separated, ten columns, no empty fields: '-' is "nothing". (A shell
# `read` with IFS=<tab> would silently merge two adjacent tabs, so an empty
# field would shift every column after it.)
#   id      scenario name; results are B-<implementation>-<id>
#   argv    the launcher's arguments, split on spaces; '-' for none
#   setup   comma list of sandbox changes and check modifiers:
#             utf16env       .env saved as UTF-16LE with a BOM (what 5.1's > writes)
#             crlfenv        .env with CRLF line endings (must still work)
#             latin1env      .env also holds a Latin-1 byte (0xE9) and no NUL:
#                            still plain text, must still work
#             crlf-mvnw      home-crew-user-service/mvnw has CRLF line endings
#             crlf-reload    dev-reload.sh has CRLF line endings
#             nodocker       PATH has no docker at all (the run is refused, not
#                            risked, if a real docker is still reachable)
#             cwd-root       run from the infra checkout as ./dev (.\dev.ps1)
#             hostile-sp     the checkouts live under 'hc cli [x]'
#             hostile-u      the checkouts live under 'hc-' + e-acute (U+00E9),
#                            generated at run time so this file stays ASCII
#             sh-only        ./dev only (sh, dash, busybox, gitbash, wsl)
#             expect-msys    every docker call must see MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 and
#             hijack         dev.ps1 runs under -Command with a `docker`
#                            FUNCTION defined; it must still call the fake .exe
#   env     KEY=VALUE;KEY=VALUE for the fake (see test/cli/fake-docker.sh):
#   exit    the launcher's exit code, exactly
#   calls   the docker calls, in order, ';'-separated, each argv joined by one
#           space; '-' for none. Separately, every `compose -f ...` call must
#           run with the infra checkout as its working directory (the -f paths
#           are relative on purpose), in every scenario.
#   stderr  '(empty)' = stderr must be empty; '-' = not checked; otherwise
#           '|'-separated substrings that must all appear. Paths are compared
#           after normalisation: the sandbox becomes <ROOT> (the infra
#           checkout), <SIB> (the directory holding all the checkouts) or
#           <BASE>, and '\' becomes '/'. Only wording the two launchers share
#           is used (dev says `cp`, dev.ps1 says `Copy-Item`, and so on).
#   stdout  '|'-separated substrings of stdout; a leading '!' means "must NOT
#   info    every '==> ' line on stdout, in order, '|'-separated; '-' = there
#   req     requirement ids (R9 CLI parity, R1 the Maven volume lifecycle)
# Across implementations (B-PARITY-<id>) the exit code, the calls with their
# working directories, and the '==>' lines must be identical.
# Rows that pin a defect this table has found, so that it stays fixed:
#   help-title         dev.ps1's help once skipped its first header line (a
#                      shebang in ./dev, but the title in dev.ps1)
#   env-latin1         ./dev once ran `tr` in the user's locale: BSD tr in a
#                      UTF-8 locale stops at the first byte that is not UTF-8,
#                      and a valid .env was refused as "UTF-16"
#   up-compose-stderr  compose writes its progress to stderr; under Windows
#                      PowerShell 5.1 with stderr captured, an unguarded native
#                      call turns that into a terminating error
# Both launchers are case-sensitive, as ./dev is: `UP` is an unknown command
# switch and -contains ignore case unless told otherwise.
# missing-xp checks for <SIB> but not the quoting around it: ./dev prints
# cd "<SIB>" and dev.ps1 cd '<SIB>', each right for its own shell.
